name: Museum of Contemporary Art Yinchuan
known: Hosted the first Yinchuan Biennale in 2016, curated by Bose Krishnamachari with 73 artists (The Art Newspaper, 2016).

name: Fragmentos, Espacio de Arte y Memoria
Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá
known: Opened in February 1963 under the art historian and critic Marta Traba, who became its director.
March 2026 row over curator Eugenio Viola's dismissal, nepotism and labour claims (170 signatories).

name: Lugar a Dudas
known: The history page does not name the founders.

name: Casa Tres Patios (C3P)
known: Global Voices (2014) says the house was founded by Tony Evanko and has offered artists and local communities a space since 2006.
In 2014 Global Voices described a hackerspace, Un/Loquer, operating inside the house, and residencies for artists, architects and curators.

name: Museo de Antioquia
known: Began in 1872 as the Museo de Zea, founded by Manuel Uribe Ángel, Antonio José Restrepo and Martín Gómez.

Director María del Rosario Escobar said pre-pandemic figures had not yet been reached (El Colombiano, Kirvin Larios, "La cultura en Medellín tiene agenda 2023, pero pide más respaldo", 9 January 2023).

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM)
known: Director María Mercedes González resigned after thirteen years in October 2025 and joined the board.
The museum's site lists Rafael Tamayo Franco as director general.

name: Museo de Arte Costarricense (MAC)
known: Director in 2026: Katrin Aason Bucher (La Nación, 1 October 2026).

Its administrative board is chaired by Sally Molina Villalobos, vice minister of culture; the other members are Daniel Francisco Brenes Morales, Carola Fumero Araya, Gary Hior Hidalgo Rodríguez, Adriana Jiménez Beeche, María Otárola Luna and Emmanuel Rodríguez Chaves.

name: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo

Directors are chosen jointly by the Ministry and the board of the Fundación ProMADC;
Spanish Wikipedia lists Paz Monge Cortés as director since 2020 and Daniel Soto Morúa as chief curator since 2016.

name: TEOR/éTica
known: Founded in 1999 on the initiative of the artist, curator and researcher Virginia Pérez-Ratton (1950 to 2010).

Pérez-Ratton was the first director of the Museum of Contemporary Art and Design (MADC) in San José from 1994 to 1998, received the Prince Claus Award in 2002 and Costa Rica's Magón National Prize for Culture in 2009, and died on 6 October 2010 (Wikipedia).

name: WHW (What, How & for Whom) / Galerija Nova
known: Curatorial collective and non-profit programme in Zagreb.

Wider work: the 11th Istanbul Biennial (2009), the Croatian pavilion at the 54th Venice Biennale (2011) and, for Ćurlin, Ilić and Sabolović, the artistic directorship of Kunsthalle Wien from June 2019 to June 2024 and of Skulptur Projekte Münster 2027 (WHW).
